newsitem.title: CHINA: HK braces for worst tropical storm threat in years.
newsitem.headline: HK braces for worst tropical storm threat in years.

text.p: A typhoon bore down on Hong Kong on Saturday, threatening to be the worst for years, severely disrupting air traffic and shipping and forcing emergency precautions to be introduced.
The territory of 6.4 million people rushed supermarkets as rain pelted down, scurried for cover and battened down hatches for a long stay indoors. Roads were clogged as workers headed home.
The Hong Kong Observatory hoisted typhoon warning signal eight at noon (0400 GMT), which means that winds with speeds of 63 to 117 km an hour (40 to 74 mph) are expected in the territory.
A spokesman at the observatory said it was possible that Typhoon Victor would make a direct hit on Hong Kong.
At noon the storm was centred about 170 km (100 miles) south of Hong Kong and forecast to move north at about 18 km per hour (11 mph) towards the Pearl River estuary, the observatory said.
Victor was expected to make a landfall near the estuary at around midnight (1600 GMT). Hong Kong is located at the far eastern edge of the estuary.

Victor, threatening to come closest to Hong Kong of any typhoon in recent years, forced 15 flights to be diverted and more diversions were expected in the next few hours, a spokesman for Hong Kong's Civil Aviation Department told Reuters.
Ferry services to outlying islands and to neighbouring Portuguese-ruled Macau were cancelled because of the bad weather.
The Hong Kong government urged people to take precautions, board up windows and doors and advised workers to go home. Schools were closed and government employees sent home.
